function: CSI feedback with channel prediction: Transformer encoder predicts future downlink geometric channel parameters, quantized and fed back; Transformer decoder reconstructs the channel matrix at the BS (p. 5).
system: FDD MIMO-OFDM downlink, BS with 64 antennas, UE with one antenna, 28 GHz, 100 MHz, 1024 subcarriers; no RIS (p. 9, Table II).
method: Transformer encoder and decoder (multi-head self-attention, fully connected and 2D convolution layers), trained supervised with NMSE loss; parameter-selective bit allocation derived analytically (p. 5-9).
data_channel: Simulated channels generated with "the ray-tracing method described in 3GPP TR 38.901" at 28 GHz; 80,000 training, 20,000 validation, 20,000 test samples; urban and rural variants (p. 9, 11-12).
test_conditions: Training at v = 3 km/h; 60 and 108 km/h also tested, retraining unstated; urban/rural: "tested scenario is different from the training scenario" (p. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: LASSO, DLRec (least squares with angular-delay reciprocity). Learned: CsiNet, TransNet, CVNN, Pruning, PTNet, CsiNet-LSTM; also parametric feedback with uniform bit allocation (p. 9-10).
metrics: Channel NMSE, cosine similarity between reconstructed and true channel, and BER with QPSK and hard decoding (p. 10-11).
complexity: none; only the feedback compression ratio 4L/(2NfNt) is stated (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 9: "We generate the channel using the ray-tracing method described in 3GPP TR 38.901"
q2_support: p. 12: "COMPaCT works well even when the tested scenario is different from the training scenario"
q3_support: p. 9: "LASSO [30], a well-known compressive sensing (CS)-based approach" and "CsiNet [12], which uses a CNN-based autoencoder"; p. 10: "COMPaCT achieves a reduction of more than 3.5 dB in NMSE over CsiNet"; "Even when compared to DLRec, the NMSE gain of COMPaCT is more than 1.5 dB"
q4_support: p. 5: "the compression ratio of the proposed COMPaCT is" 4L/(2NfNt), a feedback-overhead figure only; no FLOPs, parameter count, or runtime of COMPaCT is reported anywhere in the paper
q5_support: p. 9: "We generate the channel using the ray-tracing method described in 3GPP TR 38.901"; channels are self-generated, no code or data link is given, and no public dataset or measurement is used
notes: Included: area 2 (CSI feedback with prediction); BS has 64 antennas and UE one (Nr = 1, p. 3), so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. q1: the channel model of Eq. (2) draws angles, delays and path losses from uniform distributions and Table II cites Samimi and Rappaport [29]; Fig. 12 varies urban and rural path loss models of 3GPP. The paper states that the channel follows the ray-tracing method of TR 38.901, so q1 is marked met, but the reviewer should confirm that the simulator is built on TR 38.901 and not only its path loss. q2: the single sentence on p. 12 is the explicit statement; the Fig. 12 legend (combine, rural, urban) does not show which training set was used for each curve, and Figs. 8 and 13 do not say whether the models were retrained per speed, so the reviewer should confirm.
